scope: Bounded source and English-coverage review of Qurtubi's anonymous fifteenth listed interpretation of al-Kawthar as the five prayers; distinguish verse 108:1 from parallel readings of verse 108:2.

source_anchors.locator: online passage for Sura 108:1, interpretation list, displayed lines 48-50
source_anchors.witness: وقيل : الفقه في الدين . وقيل : الصلوات الخمس ; وهما الرابع عشر والخامس عشر . وقال ابن إسحاق : هو العظيم من الأمر
source_anchors.finding: The five-prayers opinion is anonymous under وقيل and follows Q04L; the paired ordinal wording places it as item 15. No speaker or route is named in this sentence.

source_anchors.locator: Sura 108:2, edition-bearing text, printed pp.376-377; displayed lines 118-124
source_anchors.witness: قوله: ﴿فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ﴾ يعني الصلوات الخمس في قول مقاتل ...
source_anchors.finding: This is a parallel interpretation of the verse-2 command to pray, explicitly attributed to Muqatil and Ibn Abbas (with the edition's note that an Ata-route phrase is absent in witness A). It is not Qurtubi's anonymous verse-1 al-Kawthar opinion.

Ibn al-Jawzi attributes a five-prayers interpretation of verse 108:2 to Muqatil. This corroborates that a related verse-2 interpretation circulated with attribution, but does not identify Qurtubi's anonymous verse-1 clause.

source_anchors.locator: vol.6, printed pp.354-355, Sura 108:1 interpretation list (cross-checked in prior Q04L checkpoint)
source_anchors.finding: The inspected nine-item list ends at رفعة الذكر and does not provide the Qurtubi Q04M wording or its speaker. This one comparator's omission is not evidence of absence from all earlier sources.

source_comparison.qurtubi_claim_boundary: Q04M is only the anonymous Qurtubi 108:1 clause وقيل الصلوات الخمس, counted as the fifteenth opinion; do not join it to adjacent Q04L or to the named Ibn Ishaq opinion after it.
source_comparison.cross_verse_boundary: Al-Wahidi and Ibn al-Jawzi explicitly associate the five-prayers meaning with Qurtubi's next-verse command فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ (108:2). The referent and verse differ from Qurtubi Q04M, where al-Kawthar (108:1) is being interpreted.
source_comparison.translation_boundary: The stored English row omits this late listed opinion. Record as an omission/coverage gap; do not insert a translation or change the row without independent review and approval.
source_comparison.route_boundary: Qurtubi's Q04M sentence supplies no isnad or reporter; do not import the parallel works' attribution or route into the Qurtubi source record.
source_comparison.inference_limit: A shared gloss on adjacent verses is a semantic parallel, not proof that Qurtubi borrowed from, or meant to attribute his anonymous clause to, Muqatil.
